mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the cost of capital and stimulates equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above a 0.2 percentage point rise over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has increased by more than 0.2pp over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in monthly payroll growth and rise in unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS growth is negative and UNRATE rises by more than 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by a 0.5 percentage point rise in the federal funds rate over three months), the increased cost of borrowing and reduced liquidity lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has risen by more than 0.5pp over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly housing starts signals strong consumer demand for residential construction, which boosts related industries and overall economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 100.5 (the 2017=100 index) indicates a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain activity, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100.5.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and decline in industrial production indicates a monetary tightening coinciding with a supply shock, which severely dampens economic activity and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.2pp and INDPRO falls by more than 0.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 4.5%), the weak labor market suppresses consumer spending and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is above 4.5%.
